THE LOCAL MEANING

What it is.

A named Columbia River estuary salmon fishery shared by Oregon and Washington. Kings means Chinook; silvers means coho. The Buoy 10 name identifies a regulated fishing area, so an ordinary Columbia River plan needs more detail before it fits this trip.

10 tips for Buoy 10 fishing | Oregon Department of Fish & Wildlife ↗Hatchery Chinook only for Buoy 10 anglers Aug. 25-Sept. 2 after strong early season | Oregon Department of Fish & Wildlife ↗Columbia River Fishing | Oregon Dept of Fish & Wildlife ↗

How it is fished.

Troll bait or lures.

The documented approach uses trolled bait or lures. Ask which launch, estuary area, and target the captain plans to use. August to mid-September is a cited window, but in-season notices can change the available opportunity. Read the current area notice rather than treating a past report as an opening.

Planning format: Full day; estuary boat. Confirm the actual duration with the provider.

EDITORIAL PREPARATION ADVICE

What to bring.

  • A warm wind layer and waterproof shell for an exposed estuary.
  • Deck shoes and a compact bag that stays clear of working rods.
  • Personal fishing equipment only after the captain specifies the trolling system.

Before you go.

Can a season notice change during the Buoy 10 run?

Yes. The research includes an in-season change. Check the current Columbia-area notices close to the trip, and ask the captain which notice covers the intended date.

What seasonal window does the evidence support?

August to mid-September is the cited fishing window. A seasonal account does not confirm current availability. Use the linked authority for current rules.

What must I confirm before I book this trip?

Confirm rods, bait, release gear, and suitable personal flotation equipment. Ask how the crew identifies the fish covered by the current rules. Confirm the tide-based departure plan and what happens if conditions change. Castward has no confirmed guide inventory for this trip type.
